objective: Explain the complete AI-assisted slide drafting architecture and how free visual generation connects to editable reconstruction.

explicit_human_constraints.text: Use a five-stage left-to-right process because sequence is part of the authored meaning.
Show Stage 2, Stage 4, and Stage 5 internal branches.
Keep relevant technologies visibly attached to the activities they enable.
Do not generate the configured footer region.

exact_content.title: Proposed Architecture for AI-Assisted Slide Drafting
exact_content.subtitle: High-quality editable slides can be produced by letting AI freely design within the right semantic and brand context, then systematically translating the generated visual back into clean, reusable PowerPoint objects.

stages.label: Communication & Semantic Planning
content: Determine content structure, relationships, hierarchy and emphasis
Produce layout-agnostic visual intent unless the user explicitly specifies layout

stages.label: Reference Retrieval
content: Style Rules (Configured typography, color system and visual conventions)

stages.label: Visual Generation
content: GPT Image 2 receives semantic visual intent, visual references, selected assets and style rules
GPT Image 2 determines visual structure, use of supplied assets, creation of new visual elements and final composition

stages.label: Parallel Understanding of the Generated Image
content: Semantic Mapping (VLM) determines what each rendered element represents and maps known assets
Pixel-Level Measurement (OpenCV + SAM 2) measures positions, boundaries, colors, strokes and text-block geometry

stages.label: Editable PowerPoint Reconstruction
content: Known Element Reconstruction uses canonical assets, native PowerPoint objects and the Known Element Library
New / Redesigned Element Reconstruction uses semantic decomposition, standard PowerPoint shapes and connectors, geometry fitting, and raster only when required
